headline: test71: 1,024/1,024 -> 1,024/1,025 by adding the single cardinality row c1025: sum(x) <= 12, justified by a Plotkin Hamming-label counting bound over 11-bit even-parity labels. The certificate is 3 identity claims + 3 points; its delivered text form is 5.47x its binary form, almost entirely because 16,390 literal obligations and a 1,024-entry identity map are pretty-printed.
reformulation: Exact optimality-preserving strengthening: target = source plus one valid inequality (sum of all 1,024 binaries <= 12). Integer feasible set and objective unchanged (both optima -12); the LP relaxation is strictly strengthened (the uniform point x=1/56 is feasible in source with objective -128/7 and violates the new row by 44/7), and the new row makes the target LP bound exactly -12, attained by an explicit 12-coordinate integer witness. Original 1,024 vars / 1,024 rows / 57,344 nonzeros -> 1,024 vars / 1,025 rows / 58,368 nonzeros.
claim_class: 3 claims, all with the same 1,024-pair identity projection: forward source->target integer identity with input_objective_lower -12 and inverse=claim 1; reverse target->source integer identity with inverse=claim 0; reverse target->source LP identity (integer modes off, inverse null) with input_objective_lower -12. Plus 3 point claims: source LP point (x=1/56, objective -128/7) requested as Strictness for inclusion_claim 2, and the 12-coordinate integer witness requested twice as Feasible (source integer, target LP) with objective -12.
claims: 3 claims in cases/test71/request.json, written by hand as a literal table at tools/prepare_test71.py:32-35: forward integer identity (projection [[i,i]] for all 1,024 coordinates, objective 'Equal', inverse=1, input_objective_lower '-12'), reverse integer identity (inverse=0), reverse LP identity (input_integers/output_integers false, inverse None, input_objective_lower '-12').

Forward claim obligations (measured from proof.rpa): 6,147 checks = VarLower/VarUpper/VarInt/RowUpper x1,024 + 2,049 'Exact' + 2 {'Local':0}; the sole step is Plotkin{id:0,bits:11,distance:6,variables:[1024 (coordinate,label) pairs],cliques:[1024 row refs]} (tools/prepare_test71.py:42).

Reverse claims replay the same families (6,145 and 4,098 checks); only the LP direction omits VarInt, and its objective bound -12 is discharged by {'RowUpper':new_index} on the added row instead of by the Plotkin local fact (tools/prepare_test71.py:59).

Point claims bind to model indices by hand: source LP strictness point at inclusion_claim 2 with all 1,024 coordinates '1/56' (:62-63), and the 12-coordinate witness from output/geometry_certificate.json -> optimal_binary_witness (x1,x579,x474,x693,x537,x451,x409,x655,x776,x828,x621,x761) requested as Feasible target=false/integers=true and target=true/integers=false, both with objective -12.

Semantics the caller must get right and the format only partially enforces: input_objective_lower is conditional on restrictions (docs/CURRENT_FORMAT.md:431, docs/OBJECTIVE_LEVEL_DESIGN.md:41), and the Strictness point must name the claim whose containment is strict (here the reverse LP claim, index 2).
proof_encoding: proof.rpa = 'RPA 3\n' + one JSON certificate (tools/prepare_test71.py:102): 1,666,672 B / 89,214 lines, versus proof.rpx 304,420 B -> 5.47x. Re-serialising the same parsed certificate compactly gives 415,264 B, so json.dumps(indent=2) accounts for 4.01x and JSON-vs-binary for the remaining 1.36x.

1,143,694 B (68.6%) of the shipped file is leading indentation whitespace. Per-section (pretty): block0 488,684 B = steps 99,768 + map 94,124 + checks 138,981; block1 374,474 B; block2 311,120 B; claims 129,056 B; points 37,293 B.

Compact attribution (measured): checks 227,475 B over 16,390 entries in 6 kinds (VarLower 3,072, VarUpper 3,072, VarInt 2,048, RowUpper 3,073, Local 2, bare 'Exact' 5,123); the 1,024-expression identity map is byte-identical in all three blocks (37,803 B each = 113,409 B = 27.3% of the compact form); Plotkin labels 10,624 B + clique refs 17,323 B; claims 30,598 B; points 15,589 B.

The case ships 10 attack artifacts next to the certificate: 5 mutated RPA/RPX pairs (missing_cliques, duplicate_label, false_strictness, wrong_optimum_point, missing_objective_bound), each also written with indent=2 (tools/prepare_test71.py:115-120).
request.json is {claims, points:[claim]} only (tools/prepare_test71.py:103), 154,037 B pretty vs 30,785 B compact (5.0x) - it re-encodes what the RPA already carries.
agent_manual_work: Wrote a complete exact MPS parser (fixed whitespace fields, fractions) and then a second, independent parser in output/verify_artifacts.py that reads the observed 10-character/24-character column fields, rejects unhandled sections and bound types, and re-checks both the source and the written artifact (digest eval 'Independently auditing generated model and certificates').

Recovered the 11-bit even-parity labelling from incidence alone (root neighbour star cliques, edge common-neighbour profile {0:1,7:8}, BFS distance formula), then verified all 1,024 rows against predicted Hamming-distance-<=2 supports and all 523,776 unordered pairs (digest evals 'Recovering and verifying binary geometry', 'Proving cardinality bound and tightness').

Built the target by hand: inserted 1 ROWS record before COLUMNS, one coefficient record for c1025 after every column's records inside the INTORG/INTEND region, and 1 RHS record before BOUNDS - 1,026 inserted records with all 61,449 source records retained in order (digest eval 'Writing single committed reformulation'; report section 5).

Constructed the tightness witness without a solver: order-12 Paley/Hadamard construction over Z_11 with entry-by-entry orthogonality, normalisation, removal of the constant coordinate, mapping the 12 words to variable names, then direct evaluation of all 1,024 rows (672 loads = 1, 352 = 0, objective -12).

Hand-computed the remaining arithmetic: uniform point 1/56 with own-row load 14/5, source LP objective -128/7, target violation residual 44/7, and the maximum distinct-row overlap 20 (so no original row is continuously implied even after the cut).
preparer_helpers: tools/prepare_test71.py is 127 physical lines (case index: 126) and imports 4 helpers from 2 sibling preparers: parse_mps and row_ref (tools/prepare_affine.py:20,77) and expression, expr_json, sha (tools/prepare_test40.py:72,81,147); it defines 6 things of its own (evaluate, certificate, main + locals).

Hand-rolled exact point oracle evaluate(model, point, integer) at tools/prepare_test71.py:16-28, returning {'objective', 'violations':[{kind,index,residual}], 'checked_variables', 'checked_rows'} - the ground truth for five evaluations (source/target relaxed and integer) asserted at :94-96.

Hand-rolled the obligation list: identity projection (:32), 1,024-entry identity map built as expr_json(expression(0,{i:1})) (:36), per-variable and per-row check appends (:43-58), and the objective-bound marker {'RowUpper':new_index} / {'Local':0} (:59).

Hand-rolled the Plotkin premises: labels read from output/geometry_certificate.json (:79-80), 1,024 clique refs via row_ref(a, name) (:42), and an independent Python re-verification that every pair at Hamming distance < 6 shares an actual row (:86-89, histogram in independent_exact_checks.json).

Wrote the caller contract itself as {'claims': cert['claims'], 'points': [p['claim'] for p in cert['points']]} (:103) and encoded the five required rejections as deep-copied mutations with per-mutation 'rule_broken' prose (:113-123).
friction: Text form costs 5.47x the binary: indent=2 is 68.6% of the 1,666,672 B RPA. Corpus check: exactly 4 of 80 delivered RPAs are pretty-printed (test28, test40, test71, test84; writers at tools/prepare_test28.py, :95 of prepare_test84.py, :102 of prepare_test71.py) and they are exactly the 4 highest RPA/RPX ratios (6.64/5.85/5.59/5.47); all 76 compact ones top out at 1.86.

Every obligation is written out literally: 16,390 check entries for one identity correspondence (1,024 coordinates + 1,024 rows + 1 new row), and the same 1,024-expression map appears in all three blocks (113,409 B = 27.3% of the compact form) although claims share it.

Plotkin premises are supplied exhaustively rather than minimally: 1,024 clique refs (17,323 B compact) where only coverage is required (docs/FORMAT_V3.md:18), and the coverage scan costs n^2*ceil(r/64) = 16,777,216 word ops at r=1,024 versus 2,097,152 at r=128 (the 197,120 close pairs / 1,540 pairs per row counting bound, 197120/1540 = 128 exactly); the kernel performs no clique discovery (docs/FORMAT_V3.md:44).

The 5 negative checks assert only status=='INVALID' (tools/prepare_test71.py:122), so a mutation rejected by an unrelated obligation counts as success - the freshly added code/location fields are never asserted.

The preparer can only re-derive the edit rather than consume it: it re-parses both MPS files, counts rows to find the single new row, and asserts sense/rhs/terms from scratch (:76-78), because the agent's construction exists only as spliced MPS text.
notes: Why text is 5x binary here: the gap is representation, not mathematics. Measured decomposition of 5.47 = 4.01 (json.dumps(indent=2) whitespace on ~20,000 single-entry objects) x 1.36 (JSON key strings and decimal rationals vs the RPX's compact step/check encoding). The certificate is small in substance: 6 obligation kinds, 3 claims, one added row. [INFERENCE] with a range/batch encoding and a compact writer, the emitted text would be close to the genuinely case-specific data (Plotkin labels 10,624 B + clique refs 17,323 B), i.e. ~20x smaller, and the per-coordinate domain/row obligations could be derived from the edit record instead of enumerated. Implication for any RPA-emitting API: it must (a) never pretty-print, (b) own batch/range and identity-map forms, and (c) report estimated bytes and rule work before assembly, because the 256 MiB text budget is otherwise spent ~4x early and because kernel work scales with the caller's clique-list size. Case context: solver-blind run, 13 turns / 12 tool calls / 0 failures / 332.7 s / $0.21; 8 eval cells, 31,669 chars of eval code, hand-rolled Fraction/collections/hashlib only; preparation.json status VERIFIED, rpa_bytes 1,666,672, preparation_seconds 1.03 excluding the 4 kernel runs (canonical source/target, assemble, verify). docs/FORMAT_V3.md:5 records test71 as the motivation for the V3 Plotkin inference and input_objective_lower contract, so this case's capability demands are load-bearing for the format itself.
